title: Revamp prefetch state machine and compact session index
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem: The current continuous-batcher prefetch logic stores rich metadata inline with KV entries and couples lease/heartbeat logic into the hot path. This causes cache fragmentation, high per-session allocation counts, and tail latency spikes during prefetch churn. Several incidents (see INC-2025) showed worst-case memory growth under synthetic multiplexer workloads.

Goal: Separate prefetch control state from the raw KV payload and introduce a compact session index to reduce per-session allocations. Move long-running lease arbitration and heartbeat drivers off the fast token path into a lightweight coordinator. The end result should be: 1) lower p50/p95 latency under high churn, 2) reduced resident set size for typical chat workloads, and 3) simpler scheduler invariants to make future prefetch optimizations safer.

Approach:
- Introduce a compact session index (dense int -> session ref) stored in a slab-backed arena to avoid heap fragmentation.
- Replace inline prefetch metadata objects with 16-byte compact descriptors that reference the session index.
- Extract lease/heartbeat flows into a coordinator threadpool with bounded work-queues and backpressure tokens.
- Add a prefetch state machine with explicit states (Idle, Pending, InFlight, Stale) and a deterministic transition table to simplify reasoning and tests.
- Add observability: prefetch state histograms, descriptor allocation rate, compact-index load factor, coordinator queue depth.

Trade-offs: small additional indirection on cache hits (one integer lookup) versus large savings in allocation count and fragmentation. Coordinator adds a soft dependency on the new bounded-threadpool library (libtaskpool v1.2) — plan includes a staged upgrade and feature-flag rollout.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- End-to-end regression tests for state transitions (unit + integration).
- Canary on dedicated capacity with synthetic churn workload shows >=10% RSS reduction and <=2% regression on median latency.
- No increase in 95th token latency in production canary.
- Metrics and dashboards added for new observability signals.

Rollout plan: feature-flag guarded; start with internal canary on dev-dedicated pool, then slow rollout to 10% of customers, then full ramp if no regressions after 72 hours.
acceptance_criteria: Prefetch state transitions covered by unit tests and integration harness
Compact session index reduces per-session allocations by at least 40% in bench profile
Canary shows >=10% RSS reduction under churn workload
No increase in p95 token latency on canary (hard stop)
New prefetchtable and coordinator metrics surfaced in Console (prefetch_descriptors, compact_index_load, coordinator_queue_depth)
